newsitem.title: USA: U.S. envoy heads to Europe for fresh talks on Cuba.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy heads to Europe for fresh talks on Cuba.

text.p: Undersecretary of Commerce Stuart Eizenstat headed for Europe on Thursday to discuss European resistance to tighter U.S. economic sanctions against Cuba's communist government.

Eizenstat, who was assigned by President Bill Clinton to persuade U.S. trading allies to make common cause in pressing Cuban leader Fidel Castro to undertake democratic reforms, has so far met stiff opposition to the controversial Helms-Burton law aimed at discouraging foreign investment in Cuba.
Eizenstat plans to visit Amsterdam, Rome, The Hague, Copenhagen and Brussels during his latest mission, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
It is one of a number of trips the U.S. envoy has made to Europe, Canada and Mexico on the issue.
Eizenstat expects to meet government officials, business executives and private humanitarian groups during his week-long trip, Burns said.

Discussions will focus on Helms-Burton, a law named after its Republican sponsors that allows lawsuits to be filed in U.S. courts against foreign firms that own or operate properties confiscated by Cuba after its 1959 revolution from U.S. citizens or Cubans who are now U.S. citizens.

The law also allows the United States to deny entry visas to executives of firms profiting from those properties, as well as their families, a punishment already imposed on a Canadian mining firm and a Mexican telecommunications company.
Mexico and Canada have passed retaliatory legislation, while the European Union is challenging the U.S. measure before the World Trade Organisation.
In July Clinton suspended for six months the toughest provision allowing U.S. claimants to sue foreign investors doing business with confiscated property in Cuba.
On his European mission, Eizenstat will also discuss how to support human rights groups in Cuba "whose rights are being taken away by the Castro government," Burns said.
